articles.title: More than 1 in 10 chance AI ‘could kill all humans,’ says Anthropic safety lead after colleague quits
articles.snippet: A senior Anthropic safety researcher has said there is more than a 10 percent chance artificial intelligence "could kill all humans" by the end of the decade, just hours after a colleague resigned over fears the AI lab and its rivals are carelessly racing to build "superhuman systems" they cannot control. In a post on X announcing his departure, Jacob Coxon, a researcher who has trained AI systems at Anthropic, said he had quit the company over its lax approach to safety. Coxon, who previously trained systems for OpenAI, accused the two AI companies of "racing straight to self-improving superi
articles.summary: Anthropic safety lead estimates a >10% chance AI could 'kill all humans' by 2030, following a colleague's resignation over concerns about reckless racing toward superhuman systems.

articles.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous AI alignment efforts have focused primarily on first-order social norms -- teaching models what is socially acceptable or unacceptable (e.g., `do not steal'). However, social intelligence depends not only on norm recognition, but also on anticipating who will enforce it and how (e.g., public shame or even imprisonment). These second-order expectations, known as metanorms, govern how people respond when social rules are broken. articles.summary: This paper introduces a framework for evaluating metanorm reasoning in LLMs—second-order social expectations about how people respond when rules are broken. It aims to move beyond first-order norms like 'do not steal' to capture deeper social intelligence.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個評估 LLM 中 metanorm 推理嘅框架——即係關於規則被打破時人哋點樣回應嘅二階社會期望。佢旨在超越好似「唔好偷嘢」呢啲一階規範，去捕捉更深層嘅社會智能。

articles.title: CriticGen: Generation-Aware Evaluation as Actionable Feedback
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluation methods for large language models are coarse-grained and decoupled from generation, producing generic explanations that fail to provide actionable feedback for model improvement. We propose CriticGen, a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. CriticGen first generates sample-specific evaluation dimensions and scoring criteria under high-level categories such as subjective, objective, and self-derived constraints. articles.summary: CriticGen is a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. It generates sample-specific evaluation dimensions and scoring criteria to provide actionable feedback for model improvement.
articles.summaryZhHK: CriticGen 係一個細粒度、generation-aware 嘅評估框架，將評估轉化為對答案改進嘅可行控制。佢生成樣本特定嘅評估維度同評分標準，為模型改進提供可行嘅反饋。

articles.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory for LLM agents is evaluated today by conversational recall benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval), which measure question answering over dialogue history, not whether remembered facts change what a tool-using agent does. We present MERIT (Memory Evaluation for Realistic Instrumented Tasks), a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of memory for task-executing agents under explicit cost accounting. articles.summary: This paper presents MERIT, a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of long-term memory for tool-using LLM agents under explicit cost accounting. It provides episodic tool-use tasks across three domains to evaluate whether remembered facts change agent behavior.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文介紹 MERIT，一個 benchmark 同 harness，用嚟喺明確成本核算下衡量長期記憶對使用工具嘅 LLM agent 嘅邊際效用。佢提供三個領域嘅 episodic tool-use 任務，評估記住嘅事實會唔會改變 agent 行為。

articles.title: AutoFyn Technical Report: Non-Parametric Expert Iteration for Long-Horizon Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce AutoFyn, an agent harness inspired by the Expert Iteration algorithm, adapting a frozen model across many rounds by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. Each round begins from a fresh model session, and durable information is reintroduced only through explicit interfaces such as persistent memory files, reports, and repository state. articles.summary: AutoFyn is an agent harness inspired by Expert Iteration that adapts a frozen model by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. It uses an orchestrator to explore and plan multiple approaches with specialized agents in each round.
articles.summaryZhHK: AutoFyn 係一個受 Expert Iteration 啟發嘅 agent harness，通過更新來自已驗證獎勵信號嘅持久狀態嚟適應 frozen model，而唔係模型權重。佢每輪用 orchestrator 同專門 agent 探索同規劃多種方法。

articles.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured post-training pruning of transformers requires selecting complete functional units whose suppression causes limited degradation. We formulate structured-unit selection for language and vision transformers as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed candidate-evaluation budget. Attention heads and MLP channel groups are temporarily masked on calibration batches. Paired damage is the masked loss minus the base loss on the same batch, reducing batch-to-batch variation. articles.summary: This paper formulates structured-unit pruning for language and vision transformers as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed evaluation budget. It masks attention heads and MLP channel groups on calibration batches, using paired damage metrics to reduce batch variation.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文將語言同視覺 transformer 嘅結構化單元剪枝，表述為固定評估預算下一個 damage-aware 多臂老虎機問題。佢喺校準批次上遮罩 attention heads 同 MLP channel groups，用 paired damage 指標嚟減少批次差異。

articles.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning and large language models often struggle to accurately capture the causal mechanics of game environments. Standard reinforcement learning agents tend to rely on spurious correlations, while large language models are prone to hallucinating game rules. Although causal reinforcement learning improves interpretability, there is currently no formal methodology to map complex game mechanics directly into causal models. To address this, we propose a deterministic framework that compiles games specified in the Video Game Descriptio
articles.summary: This paper proposes a deterministic framework that compiles games specified in the Video Game Description Language (VGDL) into causal models. It aims to improve RL and LLM agents' ability to capture the causal mechanics of game environments.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個確定性框架，將用 Video Game Description Language (VGDL) 指定嘅遊戲編譯成因果模型。佢旨在改善 RL 同 LLM agent 捕捉遊戲環境因果機制嘅能力。

articles.title: SciLitBench: Benchmark and Design Principles for LLM-Powered Systematic Literature Reviews
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systematic reviews require sustained human judgment across thousands of records, yet existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) typically examine review stages in isolation. We introduce SciLitBench, a multi-stage benchmark spanning title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and schema-guided data extraction, with 42,981 retrieved records, 1,012 full texts, and annotations for 888 included papers. Across 22 open-weight LLMs from six model families, explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria improve title and abstract screening $F
articles.summary: SciLitBench is a multi-stage benchmark for LLM-powered systematic literature reviews, covering screening and data extraction stages with over 42,000 retrieved records. Evaluation across 22 open-weight LLMs shows explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria improve title and abstract screening performance.
articles.summaryZhHK: SciLitBench 係一個用於 LLM 驅動系統性文獻回顧嘅多階段 benchmark，涵蓋篩選同數據提取階段，有超過 42,000 條檢索記錄。對 22 個 open-weight LLM 嘅評估顯示，明確嘅納入/排除標準可改善標題同摘要篩選表現。

articles.title: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents need to navigate visually rich, long-horizon interfaces that change across sites, yet most previous agents still learn each task in isolation and discard the procedural knowledge they accumulate. Recent skill-augmented frameworks take an important first step, but they treat the skill library as a flat or two-tier prompt-side cache and offer no principled mechanism for compressing redundancy or composing skills recursively. articles.summary: SCAFFOLD is a self-improving framework for visual web agents that induces parametric, executable skills and compresses redundancy recursively. It enables agents to accumulate procedural knowledge across tasks rather than learning each one in isolation.
articles.summaryZhHK: SCAFFOLD 係一個用於視覺網頁 agent 嘅自我改進框架，可以歸納參數化、可執行嘅技能，並遞迴壓縮冗餘。佢令 agent 可以跨任務累積程序性知識，而唔係孤立噉學每個任務。

articles.title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) impose substantial energy costs during deployment, yet current compression methods apply uniform quantization across all components, risking damage to critical reasoning circuits. We present a reasoning-aware compression framework that benchmarks quantization conditions across five reasoning benchmarks, GSM8K, FOLIO, MATH-500, ProofWriter, and MuSiQue, with hardware-level GPU energy measurement; profiles per-module INT4 vulnerability across all 196-224 (layer, projection) pairs via a perturbation sweep on a held-out
articles.summary: This paper presents a reasoning-aware compression framework that benchmarks quantization conditions across five reasoning benchmarks with hardware-level energy measurement. It profiles per-module INT4 vulnerability to protect critical reasoning circuits during energy-efficient LLM deployment.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個 reasoning-aware 壓縮框架，喺五個推理 benchmark 上用硬件級能源測量嚟基準化量化條件。佢剖析每個模組嘅 INT4 脆弱性，以喺節能 LLM 部署期間保護關鍵推理電路。

articles.title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents have achieved significant success in automating complex internet tasks but deploying them in real-world environments requires continuous online adaptation. Given that deploying powerful proprietary models remains commercially cost-prohibitive, practitioners must rely on lightweight local models that evolve post-deployment via online teaching from a stronger teacher. articles.summary: This paper addresses budget-aware online adaptation for web agents, showing that trajectory-level preference optimization wastes budget on unresolvable episodes. It proposes a method for deciding when and what to teach lightweight local models from a stronger teacher.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文處理 web agent 嘅預算感知在線適應問題，顯示 trajectory-level preference optimization 會喺無法解決嘅 episodes 上浪費預算。佢提出一個方法決定幾時同教乜嘢，由較強老師教輕量本地模型。

articles.title: The Failure Happens Before the Drift: The Social Dynamics of Values in LLM Agent Societies
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly used as proxies for human participants in social science research, yet it remains unclear whether they can faithfully simulate diverse and conflicting human value systems. We present a World Values Survey (WVS)-grounded simulation framework where culturally diverse agents with different communication styles engage in longitudinal, value-laden discussions. articles.summary: This paper presents a World Values Survey-grounded simulation framework where culturally diverse LLM agents engage in value-laden discussions. Across roughly 4,000 conversations with 1,200 personas and three models, it examines social dynamics and value drift in agent societies.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個以 World Values Survey 為基礎嘅模擬框架，令文化多元嘅 LLM agent 參與充滿價值觀嘅討論。喺大約 4,000 場對話、1,200 個 persona 同三個模型中，佢檢視 agent 社會中嘅社會動力同價值漂移。

articles.title: Beyond "AI Helps Humans": Decision-Targeted Evaluation Design for Human-Agent Teams in the Agentic Era
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wherever a coding agent works under engineer supervision, or a clinical model assists a radiologist, the deployment question is whether to keep the human-AI workflow or replace it with the human alone or the agent alone. The human-AI workflow is worth keeping only if it beats both of those alternatives. articles.summary: This paper proposes decision-targeted evaluation design for human-AI teams, addressing whether to keep a human-AI workflow or replace it with human alone or agent alone. It handles fixed replay budgets by deciding which tasks to replay to observe alternative outcomes.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出人機團隊嘅 decision-targeted 評估設計，處理應唔應該保留人機工作流程，定係用純人類或純 agent 取代。佢喺固定 replay 預算下決定重播邊啲任務嚟觀察替代結果。

articles.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent memory allows LLM agents to use earlier interactions when answering new queries. Existing methods often compress interaction histories into summaries or other LLM-generated representations. Repeated generation adds cost and can discard answer-bearing details before the system knows what a future query will require. articles.summary: EdgeMem is an agent-memory method that preserves original interaction turns and organizes them through complementary content, temporal, and episodic cues via a multi-anchor hypergraph. It avoids LLM-generated summaries to reduce cost and retain answer-bearing details.
articles.summaryZhHK: EdgeMem 係一種 agent-memory 方法，保留原始互動輪次，並通過 multi-anchor hypergraph 嘅內容、時間同 episodic 線索嚟組織佢哋。佢避免用 LLM 生成摘要，以減少成本同保留帶有答案嘅細節。

articles.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paradigm of LLMs has rapidly shifted from passive language interfaces to autonomous Claw-like agents that execute long-horizon tasks across stateful workspaces. While Agentic Reinforcement Learning (Agentic RL) provides a promising path to optimize these agents, its scaling is heavily bottlenecked by the severe scarcity of interactive training environments. articles.summary: EnvCraft synthesizes executable environments for agentic RL in claw-like agents, addressing the scarcity of interactive training environments. It goes beyond tool-calling endpoints to support end-to-end real-world task demands.
articles.summaryZhHK: EnvCraft 為 claw-like agent 嘅 agentic RL 合成可執行環境，解決互動訓練環境稀缺嘅問題。佢超越 tool-calling endpoints，支援端到端真實世界任務需求。

articles.title: Agents Trust Tools Too Much: Measuring Reliance on Unreliable Tools
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing evaluations of tool-using agents primarily measure whether an agent can successfully complete diverse tasks with tools. These evaluations generally assume that tools return reliable information. However, tool returns in real-world systems can be plausible yet incorrect. We investigate how agents respond to unreliable tool returns by evaluating fourteen LLMs using three tools-web search, LLM sub-agent delegation, and code execution. articles.summary: This paper investigates how agents respond to unreliable tool returns by evaluating fourteen LLMs with three tools—web search, LLM sub-agent delegation, and code execution. It corrupts tool returns to measure whether agents adopt corrupted content in their final outputs.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文通過評估十四個 LLM 同三個工具——網頁搜索、LLM sub-agent 委派同程式碼執行——嚟研究 agent 點樣回應不可靠嘅工具回傳。佢破壞工具回傳，量度 agent 會唔會喺最終輸出中採用被破壞嘅內容。

articles.title: The Knowing-Saying Gap: When Probes See Errors that Confidence Misses
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear probes detect corrupted context in language models with near-perfect accuracy, yet this does not translate into reliable failure prediction. articles.summary: Linear probes can detect corrupted context in language models with high accuracy, but this capability does not reliably predict actual model failures, revealing a critical gap between detectability and real-world performance monitoring.

Yet, authoring SHACL shapes requires technical expertise that most domain experts lack. Translating natural language requirements into SHACL (NL2SHACL) would lower this barrier. articles.summary: NL2SHACL-Bench introduces a benchmark suite for evaluating natural language to SHACL shape translation, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation methods for this knowledge graph validation task.

articles.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern agentic AI systems combine multiple large language model agents with heterogeneous skills, yet most architectures either fix communication in advance or allow full broadcast. articles.summary: A cooperative game-theoretic approach to optimize communication and coalition formation among heterogeneous LLM agents, balancing token costs and latency in multi-agent systems.

articles.title: MetaSpace: Metamorphic Testing for Spatial Cognition in Embodied Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An embodied agent is an intelligent entity that interacts with its environment through a physical body. Currently, the evaluation of embodied agents primarily relies on two paradigms: (1) manually annotated Visual Question Answering (VQA) pairs and (2) high-level task completion metrics, such as success in navigation or manipulation. articles.summary: MetaSpace proposes metamorphic testing methods to evaluate spatial cognition in embodied agents, moving beyond task completion metrics to uncover critical vulnerabilities and safety violations.

articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM agents move from decision support to autonomous procurement, firms need to know whether delegated negotiators create value, divide it predictably, and avoid money-losing contracts. articles.title: TREAT: Evaluating Access to Formal Knowledge across Equivalent Mathematical Representations
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly operate between flexible input representations and formal objects used by downstream tools. articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous research loops driven by large language models can run machine-learning experiments at scale but tend to drift toward local refinements of whichever metric they optimise rather than testing the hypotheses that motivate the experiments. articles.title: TeXFix-Bench: An Empirically Grounded Multi-Format Benchmark for LLM-Based Document Source Repair
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific and technical writing depends on markup sources that must compile: LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown pipelines fail on missing delimiters, mismatched environments, broken imports, or package conflicts. articles.summary: TeXFix-Bench provides a multi-format benchmark for evaluating LLM-based document repair across LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown, grounded in empirically mined fault models.

articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently achieved impressive performance for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet existing approaches are primarily designed for an individual single autonomous driving agent with limited support for cooperative perception, reasoning, and planning. articles.title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2608.07622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory enables AI agents to maintain continuity across sessions, personalize behavior, and evolve through accumulated experience.
